title: Community class schedules and membership growth
audience: Yoga and Pilates instructors who run regular community classes and build membership or class-pass growth
learningOutcomes: Plan a class schedule that keeps each class inside its venue, its permit and its group size
Identify when a children's class engages a Working with Children Check category.
Grow a membership without relying on health claims, and with the consumer-law points checked
referencesAtStart: Official references for this lesson: Victorian Government, Who requires a Working with Children Check (updated 12 October 2026); Victorian Government, Working with Children Check explained (updated 24 July 2026); Working with Children Check - Victoria, business listing (no date shown; fees labelled 2026-27); Hornsby Shire Council, Commercial group fitness and personal training (no date shown); Queensland Government, Join a gym or fitness provider (last updated 23 July 2024).

instruction.heading: Building a schedule inside its limits
instruction.body: A community class schedule is a commitment to a venue and to participants. Each class must sit inside the venue's conditions, the council permit where it runs on public land, and the group size the business has set. Before adding a class to the schedule, check the venue's hours, the room size, the number of participants the room allows, and the permit for each public place. The schedule is held in {{business:jobs.scheduling_method}}. Keep the class capacity on the schedule, and do not sell a place beyond it. Where a class is moved to a new venue, the new venue's rules apply from the first session, and the permit must be checked again.

instruction.heading: Children's classes and the check categories
instruction.body: A community class for children may engage the Working with Children Check. The Victorian government's list (updated 12 October 2026) names private tutoring and coaching aimed at children (code 28), commercial gyms and play venues aimed at children (code 32), and sport, recreation and culture clubs that deal with children (code 42). The government explainer states that a clearance is valid for five years (updated 24 July 2026). A business listing that copies the government text says self-employed workers are covered and refers to direct contact with under-18s (no date shown; secondary copy). Do not offer a children's class until the position is recorded for the venue and the state.

instruction.heading: Growing membership without a health promise
instruction.body: Membership growth comes from a reliable schedule, a welcoming class, clear communication and good records of attendance. It does not come from claims that a class will cure a condition, improve a diagnosis or reduce a medical risk. Describe the class by its style, its level and its time. Membership terms must state the classes included, the period, the rule for unused classes, cancellation and refund. Queensland's fitness-agreement page (last updated 23 July 2024) sets a 48-hour cooling-off period, refunds of prepaid fees within 14 days, and a 12-month cap on prepayment, for Queensland only. Check the terms before the membership is sold, and record the check. The communication and cancellation policy is in {{business:customers.communication_policy}}, and the pricing method for memberships is in {{business:pricing.pricing_method}}.

procedure: Check the venue's hours, room size and participant limit before adding a class to the schedule
Confirm the council permit for each public place, and record the permit reference on the schedule
Set the group size for each class and do not sell a place beyond it
Before offering a children's class, check the Working with Children Check position for the class and the state, and record the result
Write the membership terms, and check them against the consumer-law position before selling
Record each class, attendance and membership change, and review the schedule each term

workedExamples.situation: An instructor plans to add a Saturday children's Pilates class in a community centre, and needs to confirm the children's check position.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Can the class be added to the schedule now?
workedExamples.reasoning: The class is for under-18s and may engage a Working with Children Check category. The Victorian list covers coaching for children, commercial gyms and play venues aimed at children, and sport, recreation and culture clubs that deal with children. The instructor should check the category for the class and the state, record the result, and then add the class. Adding it before the check is complete is not a safe decision.

workedExamples.situation: A membership advertisement says that joining the class will help members with their arthritis.
workedExamples.reasoning: The advertisement should be changed to describe the class's style, level and time, and should not refer to a condition. The change should be recorded in the review of communications.

equipmentAndPpe: Schedule with venue, room size, participant limit and permit reference for each class
Membership terms, approved by the business
Working with Children Check position record for children's classes

commonErrors.error: Selling places beyond the room or permit limit.
commonErrors.prevention: Set the capacity on the schedule and do not sell beyond it.

commonErrors.error: Running a children's class before the check position is recorded.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the category for the class and the state, and record the result before the first class.

commonErrors.error: Advertising a health outcome to grow membership.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe the class by its style, level and time. Remove any condition claim.

commonErrors.error: Selling memberships with no refund or unused-class terms.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the terms first and check them against the consumer-law position before selling.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Victoria: Working with Children Check categories 28, 32 and 42 are listed on the government page updated 12 October 2026.
Council permit conditions for classes on public land are council-specific.
A schedule, a membership or a children's class check does not register the business or grant a permit or a licence.

qualityStandard: Every class on the schedule has a venue, a participant limit and a permit reference where needed
Every children's class has a recorded Working with Children Check position before its first session
Every membership has written terms checked against the consumer-law position
No advertisement makes a health outcome claim
documentationEvidence: Class schedule with venue, participant limit and permit reference
Working with Children Check position record for each children's class
summary: Schedule each class inside its venue, permit and participant limit
Check the Working with Children Check position before any children's class
Grow membership with a clear schedule, not a health promise
Completing this lesson grants no permit, check or licence

knowledgeChecks.question: An instructor wants to add a children's Pilates class before checking the Working with Children Check position. What is the correct decision?
options: Add the class, since children's classes always need no check at all in any state
Add the class and check later if a parent asks about the check on the day
Check the category for the class and the state, record the result, and then add the class

knowledgeChecks.question: A membership advertisement says the class will help with arthritis. What should happen?
options: Change the advertisement to describe the class's style, level and time, without a condition claim
Run the advertisement, since members want it and the business needs it right now at the start of term
Add a small print disclaimer and run it for members this term and the next two terms
